newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE continues upward march, supply tight.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE continues upward march, supply tight.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices continued their march upward in moderate activity on Monday as demand for blending put pressure on a rapidly shrinking pool of prompt supply.
For more than a month, high production rates of reformulated gasoline has led to increased demand for MTBE, a gasoline additive used as an oxygenate and octane-enhancer.
"MTBE supply is just still very very tight," said a New York Harbor trader.
The pool of spot supply started off the summer demand season on the shallow side, due to maintenance at several refineries in May.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, the main producing hub, Houston spot MTBE was done at 93.00 cents a gallon, up a half cent from Friday. Players pegged the buy/sell range at 92.50/93.50 cents.
In the East Coast, a 50,000-barrel parcel in New York Harbor swapped hands at 98.00 cents, two cents above Friday's levels, players said.
"There is continued refinery demand for blending RFG," said a trader, adding there was little other fundamental news in the market.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631--
